ANT.bio: Born into a motorsport family in Bologna, Antonelli was scouted by Mercedes at age 12 after dominating European karting. He won back-to-back FIA Karting European Championships, then swept the Italian and ADAC F4 titles in 2022 with 22 wins. After winning the Formula Regional European Championship in 2023, he skipped F3 entirely and went straight to F2 with Prema, where he became the youngest multiple race winner in series history. Mercedes promoted him directly to F1 in 2025 as Lewis Hamilton's replacement, making him the third-youngest F1 debutant in history. In 2026, he became the youngest driver ever to lead the World Championship.

RUS.bio: Russell grew up karting alongside his older brother Benjy, who inspired his number 63. He joined the Mercedes junior programme in 2017 after presenting Toto Wolff with a PowerPoint pitch, then won both the GP3 and F2 titles at his first attempt in back-to-back seasons. He spent three years at Williams before earning a full Mercedes seat in 2022, where he claimed his maiden victory at the Brazilian GP. Known as 'Mr Saturday' for his qualifying excellence, Russell won races in Canada and Singapore during 2025 en route to his strongest championship campaign.

HAM.bio: The most decorated driver in F1 history, Hamilton was spotted by Ron Dennis at a karting event aged 10 and signed to the McLaren junior programme. After winning the GP2 title in 2006, he debuted for McLaren in 2007 alongside Fernando Alonso, nearly winning the title as a rookie. He claimed his first championship in 2008 in dramatic last-lap fashion, then joined Mercedes in 2013 and dominated the hybrid era, winning six further titles. Hamilton made a historic move to Ferrari in 2025, fulfilling a childhood dream of driving the scarlet car.

LEC.bio: Born and raised in Monaco, Leclerc was guided by his late father Hervé and family friend Jules Bianchi. After winning the GP3 title in 2016 and the F2 championship in 2017, he joined Sauber in 2018 before Ferrari promoted him alongside Sebastian Vettel. He immediately outperformed his vastly more experienced teammate and quickly became Ferrari's undisputed leader, winning in Bahrain and Monza in his debut Ferrari season. Known for his breathtaking qualifying laps, Leclerc remains one of F1's most electrifying talents.

NOR.bio: Born in Bristol to an English father and Belgian mother, Norris started karting aged eight after watching his older brother Oliver. He won the MSA Formula title in 2015, then progressed through F3 and F2 before joining McLaren in 2019 at just 19. Known for his raw speed and entertaining personality, Norris spent years as one of the fastest drivers without a win — his 15 podiums was a record before he finally triumphed at the 2024 Miami GP. He went on to claim the 2025 World Championship in a thrilling three-way battle with Oscar Piastri and Max Verstappen.

PIA.bio: Piastri grew up in Melbourne before moving to Europe to pursue his motorsport dream. He became the first driver since Nico Rosberg to win the F3 and F2 championships in consecutive seasons, taking both titles in 2020 and 2021. Despite going without an F1 seat in 2022, he famously rejected Alpine's public announcement that he'd drive for them in 2023, having already secretly signed with McLaren. He won his first Grand Prix at Hungary in 2024 and finished third in the 2025 World Championship, cementing himself as one of F1's brightest stars.

VER.bio: Son of F1 driver Jos Verstappen and Belgian karting champion Sophie Kumpen, Max was racing karts before he could ride a bike. He made his F1 debut with Toro Rosso at just 17, becoming the youngest driver ever to start a Grand Prix. Promoted to Red Bull mid-2016, he won on debut at the Spanish GP — the youngest ever race winner. After a controversial 2021 title battle with Hamilton, he dominated F1 with three consecutive championships from 2021 to 2023. His 2024 season saw him claim a fourth title despite McLaren's resurgence.

HAD.bio: Born in Paris to a Franco-Algerian family, Hadjar rose through the Red Bull junior programme after an impressive karting career. He won the Formula Regional Middle East Championship in 2023 and showed consistent pace in F2, finishing as runner-up in 2024. A product of the Red Bull Driver Academy, he made his F1 debut with Racing Bulls (formerly Toro Rosso) in 2026 alongside Arvid Lindblad, becoming one of the most promising rookies of his generation.

GAS.bio: From Rouen, Gasly rose through the Red Bull junior programme after winning the GP2 title in 2016. He made his F1 debut with Toro Rosso in 2017 and was promoted to the main Red Bull team in 2019, but struggled and was demoted back to Toro Rosso mid-season. His comeback was remarkable — he won the 2020 Italian GP at Monza for what became Alpha Tauri, one of F1's most emotional victories. Gasly joined Alpine in 2023, bringing experience and leadership to the French works team.

LAW.bio: Growing up in New Zealand, Lawson moved to Europe as a teenager to pursue his F1 dream through the Red Bull junior programme. He impressed as a stand-in for Daniel Ricciardo at AlphaTauri in 2023, performing admirably across five races with zero preparation. He earned a full-time seat with Racing Bulls in 2025 before being promoted to partner Max Verstappen at Red Bull in 2026, becoming the first New Zealander in F1 since Brendon Hartley.

BEA.bio: One of the youngest drivers on the 2026 grid, Bearman joined the Ferrari Driver Academy as a teenager after winning multiple karting titles. He made his surprise F1 debut substituting for Carlos Sainz at the 2024 Saudi Arabian GP, finishing seventh on his first outing — the youngest British driver to score points on debut. After a strong F2 season in 2024, he earned a full-time seat at Haas for 2025, confirming his status as one of Britain's most exciting young talents.

COL.bio: Colapinto hails from Argentina and became the first Argentine driver in F1 since Gastón Mazzacane in 2001 when he replaced Logan Sargeant at Williams mid-2024. His aggressive driving style and natural talent caught the attention of Alpine, who signed him for 2026. He is regarded as one of the most exciting Latin American talents to reach F1 in decades, drawing comparisons to previous Argentine greats.

LIN.bio: Born in Virginia Water to a Swedish father and British Indian mother, Lindblad is one of the most remarkable talents ever to enter F1. A Red Bull junior from a young age, he rose through Italian F4 and F3 before a meteoric jump to F2 in 2025 at just 17. He earned his Racing Bulls seat for 2026 at just 18, becoming one of the youngest drivers to race in Formula 1 and the first to debut having been born after Fernando Alonso's second world title.

SAI.bio: Son of two-time World Rally Champion Carlos Sainz, he initially resisted following his father into motorsport before dedicating himself to single-seaters. After winning the Formula Renault 3.5 title in 2014, he joined Toro Rosso alongside Max Verstappen in 2015. He progressed through Renault and McLaren before a four-year spell at Ferrari, where he claimed four race wins. Following Lewis Hamilton's arrival at Ferrari, Sainz joined Williams and has continued to be one of F1's most consistent performers.

ALB.bio: Though born in London, Albon races under the Thai flag through his mother, becoming the first Thai F1 driver since the 1950s. He was released from the Red Bull programme in 2018 but was dramatically recalled to replace Dany Kvyat mid-2019, then promoted to the main Red Bull team. After being replaced by Sergio Pérez in 2021, he made a comeback with Williams in 2022 and has been the team's cornerstone driver ever since, earning consistent points with an underdog car.

OCO.bio: Raised in Évreux in Normandy, Ocon came from a working-class family who sacrificed everything to fund his karting career, including selling the family home. He rose through the Mercedes junior programme and made his F1 debut in 2016 with Manor before joining Force India. After a year as Mercedes reserve driver in 2019, he joined Renault/Alpine and claimed his first and only F1 victory at the 2021 Hungarian GP in chaotic conditions. He moved to Haas in 2026 as the team's experienced leader.

BOR.bio: A product of the McLaren Driver Academy from São Paulo, Bortoleto climbed the junior ranks rapidly after success in karting. He won the F3 championship in 2023 and the F2 title in 2024 — the same progression path as Oscar Piastri. Despite being a McLaren junior, he was signed by Audi for 2026, becoming a key part of the German manufacturer's Formula 1 project as they prepare for the new regulations era.

ALO.bio: The oldest driver on the 2026 grid and one of F1's greatest legends, Alonso was racing karts at age three, pushed by his father who entered him in competitions without his knowledge. He made his F1 debut with Minardi in 2001 before joining Renault, where he won back-to-back World Championships in 2005 and 2006 — the youngest double champion at the time. His subsequent career took him to McLaren, Ferrari, and back to Renault/Alpine before joining Aston Martin in 2023, where he demonstrated he remains one of F1's finest racers well into his forties.

STR.bio: Born in Montreal to billionaire entrepreneur Lawrence Stroll, Lance showed genuine talent from an early age, winning the Italian F4 title and Formula 3 European Championship before reaching F1. He joined Williams in 2017, aged just 18, and scored a surprise podium at the Azerbaijan GP in his rookie season. After Lawrence Stroll purchased Force India to create Racing Point (now Aston Martin), Lance joined the family team and has remained there since, partnering Alonso from 2023 onwards.

HUL.bio: From a small town on the German-Dutch border, Hülkenberg won the A1 Grand Prix championship for Germany before climbing through the junior ranks to F1. He became famous for holding the record for the most Grand Prix starts without a podium — a stat finally erased at the 2024 Belgian GP when he claimed his maiden podium with Haas. After years as a highly-rated midfield performer at Williams, Force India, Sauber and Renault, Hülkenberg joined Sauber/Audi for 2025 as a team leader.

BOT.bio: From the small Finnish town of Nastola, Bottas followed in the tradition of great Finnish racing drivers before him. He rose through GP3 and F2 before joining Williams in 2013. Promoted to Mercedes in 2017 to replace the retiring Nico Rosberg, he won 10 races alongside Lewis Hamilton but never claimed the title. After five years at Mercedes, he moved to Alfa Romeo/Sauber before joining Cadillac for the 2026 season as part of the American team's ambitious F1 project.

PER.bio: Known as 'Checo', Pérez came from Guadalajara and became one of Mexico's greatest sporting icons. After years of dependable but undersung performances at Sauber, McLaren and Force India/Racing Point — where he won the 2020 Sakhir GP — he earned his dream Red Bull seat in 2021. He won four races in 2023 as part of Red Bull's dominant season and claimed second in the World Championship. After a difficult 2024, he returned to Cadillac F1 for 2026 alongside Valtteri Bottas.
